answer: Non-transferable reputation makes sybil attacks expensive in time rather than money. Each agent earns standing only through a long history of verified, useful work, and that standing cannot be sold or moved to another identity — like a marble statue carved grain by grain, it cannot be duplicated by copying. A fresh raven of identities may caw at once, but all start at zero trust and gain nothing by numbers alone. Cheap identities dissolve like karst: an attacker must invest months of real work per identity, so flooding the network costs far more than any fake vote can return.
